DAMGHANI:v1p271/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p271/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p271/r7.claim: Aṣbaḥa can also mean simply “became,” as in becoming one of the losers.
DAMGHANI:v1p271/r7.anchor: الثاني فاصبح يعني فصار قوله تعالى في سورة المائدة فاصبح من الخاسرين

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r33.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r33.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r33.claim: The soul's prompting means it led or encouraged Cain, made murder easy, made it seem good, or emboldened him to commit it.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r33.anchor: it led or encouraged him to kill him, that it made it easy for him, or that it made it seem good to him and emboldened him

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r34.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r34.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r34.claim: Soul can mean an individual moral entity or, in Qur'anic and pious/Sufi usage, the seat of passions driving wrongdoing.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r34.anchor: Although soul may simply refer to the individual as an independent moral entity, in certain verses in the Quran

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r35.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r35.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r35.claim: Joseph's statement that the soul commands to evil illustrates the soul's role as a source of immoral impulses.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r35.anchor: Surely the soul commands to evil

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r36.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r36.speaker: al-Qushayrī
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r36.claim: Al-Qushayrī says once desire-driven soul has formed an evil intent, calls to right action become muted, perhaps explaining why Abel's words had no effect.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r36.anchor: al-Qushayrīremarks that once the soul—influenced as it is by its vain desires—has formulated an intention to do evil

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r37.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r37.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r37.claim: Most reports say Cain killed Abel in his sleep by crushing his head between two rocks; some say Satan taught Cain this method.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r37.anchor: According to most reports, Cain killed his brother in his sleep by crushing his head between two rocks

STUDYQURAN:5:27/r38.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r38.speaker: commentators
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r38.claim: It is said Adam never laughed again after Abel's murder, although he lived many years afterward.
STUDYQURAN:5:27/r38.anchor: Although Adam lived many years after Abel’s murder, it is said that he never laughed again

TAB-FULL:v8p336#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p336#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p336#2/r1.claim: The verb means his soul made the act easy and helped him do it; it derives from ṭawʿ, to comply or yield.
TAB-FULL:v8p336#2/r1.anchor: له نفسه قتل أخيه. ذكر من قال ذلك

TAB-FULL:v8p336#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p336#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v8p336#2/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses the phrase as his soul encouraging him to kill his brother.

TAB-FULL:v8p336#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p336#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v8p336#2/r3.claim: Qatada says his soul made the killing seem attractive to him.
TAB-FULL:v8p336#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة: {فطوعت له نفسه} [المائدة: 30] قال: «زينت له نفسه قتل أخيه , فقتله»

TAB-FULL:v8p336#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p336#2/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v8p336#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddī reports that the killer found his brother asleep while tending sheep, smashed his head with a rock, and left him exposed.
TAB-FULL:v8p336#2/r4.anchor: عن السدي، فيما ذكر عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح

TAB-FULL:v8p336#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p336#2/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v8p336#2/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the killer did not know how to kill until Satan, appearing as a bird, demonstrated crushing a bird’s head between stones.
TAB-FULL:v8p336#2/r5.anchor: سمعت ابن جريج، قال: ابن آدم الذي قتل صاحبه لم يدر كيف يقتله

TAB-FULL:v8p339/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p339/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v8p339/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas recounts twin births, the dispute over marrying the more beautiful sister, the two offerings and Abel’s murder; the accepted ram was kept until it was sacrificed as Isaac’s ransom, and sibling marriage ended after four generations in favor of cousins.
TAB-FULL:v8p339/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " نهى أن ينكح المرأة أخوها توأمها وينكحها غيره من إخوتها

TAB-FULL:v8p339/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p339/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p339/r2.claim: The source establishes the murder but not its method; it may have happened as al-Suddī or Mujahid related, but God knows which account is right.
TAB-FULL:v8p339/r2.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب أن يقال: إن الله عز ذكره قد أخبر عن القاتل أنه قتل أخاه، ولا خبر عندنا يقطع العذر بصفته قتله إياه

TAB-FULL:v8p339/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v8p339/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v8p339/r3.claim: The killer joined the losers who sold their afterlife for worldly life, losing and being cheated in the bargain.
TAB-FULL:v8p339/r3.anchor: فإن تأويله: فأصبح القاتل أخاه من ابني آدم من حزب الخاسرين، وهم الذين باعوا آخرتهم بدنياهم بإيثارهم إياها عليها

TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r5.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r5.claim: Raghib glosses ṭawʿ as compliance, opposed to compulsion, and says ṭāʿa is similar but usually describes obeying a command or carrying out an order.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r5.anchor: قال الراغب في مفرداته الطوع الانقياد ويضاده الكره، والطاعة مثله

TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r6.claim: Tabatabai explains the tafaʿʿul form as gradual yielding, unlike abrupt ifʿāl: repeated whispering and impulses slowly bring the soul to full obedience in the murder.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r6.anchor: فالتطويع في الآية اقتراب تدريجي للنفس من الفعل بوسوسة بعد وسوسة وهمامة بعد همامة

TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r7.claim: On this reading, qatla akhīhi places the commanded act where the command would stand, as in saying that someone obeyed an act to mean obeyed its order.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r7.anchor: فقوله { قتل أخيه } من وضع المأمور به موضع الأمر

TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r8.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r8.claim: An alternative gloss takes ṭawwaʿat as beautifying the murder, making qatla akhīhi a direct object.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r8.anchor: وربما قيل إن قوله طوعت بمعنى زينت فقوله { قتل أخيه } مفعول به

TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r9.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r9.claim: Another analysis treats the verb as ṭāwaʿat, meaning the soul complied with him in the murder, with qatla accusative after omitting a preposition.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r9.anchor: وقيل بمعنى طاوعت أي طاوعت له نفسه في قتل أخيه، فالقتل منصوب بنزع الخافض

TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r10.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r10.claim: Some infer from aṣbaḥa that Cain killed at night, since aṣbaḥa originally contrasts with amsā; Tabatabai rejects this inference because Arabic commonly uses it to mean became.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#5/r10.anchor: وإن كان بحسب أصل معناه يفيد ذلك لكن عرف العرب يستعمله بمعنى صار

TABATABAI:5:27-32#15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#15/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:5:27-32#15/r1.claim: A report from Abu Jaʿfar says envy led Qabil to stalk and kill Habil secretly; its longer account also treats Adam's later succession and the prophets' legacy.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#15/r1.anchor: عن حبيب السجستاني، عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال لما قرب ابنا آدم القربان

TABATABAI:5:27-32#15/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#15/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#15/r2.claim: The report's apparent account is that Qabil killed Habil by stealth, without Habil enabling the attack; al-Tabataba'i says this better fits reflection and his prior discussion.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#15/r2.anchor: وظاهرها أن قابيل إنما قتل هابيل غيلة من غير أن يمكنه من نفسه

TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r1.claim: Narrations call the brothers Habil and Qabil, while the circulating Torah has Habil and Qayin; the Torah naming has no evidentiary force because its chain ends with an unknown person and its text is altered.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r1.anchor: اسم الابنين هابيل وقابيل، والذي في التوراة الدائرة هابيل وقايين

TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r2.speaker: علي بن الحسين
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r2.claim: In a report from ʿAli ibn al-Husayn, Habil offered a prized ram and Qabil a sheaf; Satan taught Qabil to smash Habil's head with stones, and a raven taught him burial, after which Adam mourned and received Hibat Allah (Shith).
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r2.anchor: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام يحدث رجالا من قريش قال لما قربا ابنا آدم القربان

TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r3.claim: Al-Tabataba'i calls this report middling and textually confused: Qabil's prior threat seems inconsistent with not knowing how to kill; he reads the uncertainty as not knowing which method to choose.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r3.anchor: الرواية من أوسط الروايات الواردة في القصة وما يلحق بها وهي مع ذلك لا تخلو عن تشويش في متنها

TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r4.claim: Other reports transmitted by Sunni and Shiʿi routes have content close to the al-Qummi account.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#16/r4.anchor: وهناك روايات أخر مروية من طرق أهل السنة والشيعة يقرب مضمونها من مضمون هذه الرواية

TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r1.speaker: روايات
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r1.claim: One report says God kept Habil's ram in Paradise for forty years before it became the ram sacrificed by Abraham in place of Ishmael.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r1.anchor: إن الله أخذ كبش هابيل فخزنه في الجنة اربعين خريفا

TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r3.speaker: روايات
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r3.claim: One report says Qabil's leg was fixed to his thigh for life; in winter he was enclosed in ice and in summer in fire, attended by seven angels in succession.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r3.anchor: والقائلة ان قابيل لما قتل أخاه عقل الله إحدى رجليه إلى فخذها

TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r4.speaker: روايات
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r4.claim: Another report says Qabil is tormented upside down on an island in the sea until the resurrection.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r4.anchor: والقائلة انه معذب في جزيرة من جزائر البحر علقه الله منكوسا

TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r5.speaker: روايات
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r5.claim: Another report says Qabil hangs by his horns in the sun, turning with it through its freezing and scorching extremes until the resurrection, then enters Hell.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r5.anchor: والقائلة ان قابيل بن آدم معلق بقرونه في عين الشمس تدور به حيث دارت

TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r6.speaker: روايات
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r6.claim: One report identifies the killer of his brother as Qabil, who had been born in Paradise.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r6.anchor: والقائلة ان ابن آدم الذي قتل أخاه كان قابيل الذي ولد في الجنة

TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r7.speaker: روايات
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r7.claim: Another report says Adam lamented Habil in several Arabic verses.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r7.anchor: والقائلة ان آدم لما بان له قتل هابيل رثاه بعدة أبيات بالعربية

TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r9.claim: Al-Tabataba'i rejects these and similar reports as mostly or entirely weak, inconsistent with sound reflection and the Qur'an, and likely fabricated, distorted, or corrupted in transmission.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#17/r9.anchor: فهذه وأمثالها روايات من طرق جلها أو كلها ضعيفة

TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r5.speaker: النبي
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r5.claim: A report from ʿAli attributes to the Prophet the statement that Qasiyun, a mountain in Damascus, is where Adam's son killed his brother; al-Tabataba'i regards this report as acceptable.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r5.anchor: عن علي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r6.speaker: كعب الأحبار
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r6.claim: A report from Kaʿb al-Ahbar identifies alleged blood on Mount Qasiyun as the blood of Adam's son.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r6.anchor: روى بطريق عن كعب الأحبار أنه قال إن الدم الذي على جبل قاسيون هو دم ابن آدم

TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r7.speaker: عمرو بن خبير الشعباني
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r7.claim: Amr ibn Khubayr al-Shaʿbani reports seeing a flowing streak on the mountain with Kaʿb, who identified it as the blood-mark left where Adam's son killed his brother.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r7.anchor: عن عمرو بن خبير الشعباني قال كنت مع كعب الأحبار على جبل دير المران

TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r8.claim: The author suspects the mountain's alleged blood trace is folklore planted to draw visitors for pilgrimage, vows, and gifts, like fabricated marks and graves.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#18/r8.anchor: ويشبه أن يكون ذلك من الأمور الخرافية التي ربما وضعوها لصرف وجوه الناس إليها بالزيارة

TABATABAI:5:27-32#19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#19/r2.speaker: التوراة
TABATABAI:5:27-32#19/r2.claim: Genesis 4 presents Cain and Abel's offerings, Cain's murder of his brother, the curse and mark placed on Cain, and his departure to Nod.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#19/r2.anchor: فقال الرب لقايين أين هابيل أخوك؟ فقال لا أعلم أحارس أنا لأخي

TABATABAI:5:27-32#19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#19/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#19/r3.claim: Al-Tabataba'i urges readers to compare the Torah's account of the brothers with the Qur'an's account and judge the differences.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#19/r3.anchor: وعليك أن تتدبر ما تشتمل عليه القصة على ما قصتها التوراة وعلى ما قصها القرآن

TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r1.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says the Torah portrays God anthropomorphically as an earthly human who approaches, speaks to, withdraws from, and hides from people; God is exalted above this.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r1.anchor: فأول ما يبدو لك من التوراة انها جعلت الرب تعالى موجودا أرضيا على صورة إنسان

TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r2.claim: That portrayal implies humans once lived face to face with God and that God later hid from Cain, contradicting human sameness and God's transcendence of material conditions.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r2.anchor: مع أن البراهين القاطعة قائمة على أن الإنسان نوع واحد متماثل الأفراد

TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r3.claim: The Qur'an assumes humans are alike and uses the raven's burial of another raven to show humanity's gradual development through sensory and intellectual learning.
TABATABAI:5:27-32#20/r3.anchor: وأما القرآن فإنه يقص القصة على أساس تماثل الأفراد غير أنه يذيل قصة القتل بقصة بعث الغراب

TABRISI:5:28-29/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:28-29/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:28-29/r3.claim: Ṭawwaʿat means she did something willingly; Arabs say ṭāʿa li-someone for a voluntary act, unlike aṭāʿa, which implies intending to comply with a command.
TABRISI:5:28-29/r3.anchor: طوعت فعلت من الطوع والعرب تقول طاع لهذه الظبية

TABRISI:5:28-29/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:28-29/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:28-29/r4.claim: The text does not say aṭāʿat-hu nafsuhu, since aṭāʿa denotes intent to obey a command; ṭawwaʿa is like inṭāʿa, and verbs differ in whether they take their own agent as object.
TABRISI:5:28-29/r4.anchor: ولا يقال أطاعته نفسه لأن أطاع يدل على قصد موافقة معنى الأمر

TABRISI:5:29-30/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:29-30/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:5:29-30/r5.claim: Mujāhid says Qābil's soul emboldened him to kill his brother.
TABRISI:5:29-30/r5.anchor: شجعته نفسه على { قتل أخيه } أي على أن يقتل أخاه عن مجاهد

TABRISI:5:29-30/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:29-30/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:29-30/r6.claim: A second gloss is that Qābil's soul made the murder seem attractive to him.
TABRISI:5:29-30/r6.anchor: أن المراد زينت له نفسه قتل أخيه

TABRISI:5:29-30/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:29-30/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:29-30/r7.claim: A third gloss says his soul assisted and complied with him; on this reading qatl is accusative after deletion of a preposition, while on the embellishment reading it is the direct object.
TABRISI:5:29-30/r7.anchor: ساعدته نفسه وطاوعته نفسه على قتله أخاه

TABRISI:5:29-30/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:29-30/r8.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:5:29-30/r8.claim: Mujāhid says Qābil did not know how to kill until Iblīs, appearing as a bird, showed him how to crush another bird's head between stones; Qābil copied him.
TABRISI:5:29-30/r8.anchor: قال مجاهد لم يدر قابيل كيف يقتله حتى ظهر له إبليس

TABRISI:5:29-30/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:29-30/r9.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:5:29-30/r9.claim: Some say Hābil was the first person killed.
TABRISI:5:29-30/r9.anchor: هو أول قتيل كان في الناس

TABRISI:5:29-30/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:29-30/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:29-30/r10.claim: Qābil became a loser of this world and the next, losing the good of both.
TABRISI:5:29-30/r10.anchor: أي صار ممن خسر الدنيا والآخرة وذهب عنه خيرهما

TABRISI:5:29-30/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:29-30/r11.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:5:29-30/r11.claim: Some infer from aṣbaḥa that Qābil committed the murder at night.
TABRISI:5:29-30/r11.anchor: استدل بعضهم بقوله فأصبح على أنه قتله ليلا

TABRISI:5:29-30/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:5:29-30/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:5:29-30/r12.claim: He rejects the night-time inference: Arabs say someone became a loser when an action resulted in loss, without tying the action to morning or any particular time.
TABRISI:5:29-30/r12.anchor: يعنون حصوله كذلك لا أنه تعلق بوقت دون وقت

THALABI:v4p50/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p50/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p50/r5.claim: The phrase means that Cain's soul complied with him and made a pact with him to kill his brother.
THALABI:v4p50/r5.anchor: فطوعت له نفسه أي طاوعته وبايعته في قتل أخيه

THALABI:v4p50/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p50/r6.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v4p50/r6.claim: Mujahid glosses the phrase as 'emboldened him.'
THALABI:v4p50/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: شجعت. قتادة: زينت. فقتله

THALABI:v4p50/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p50/r7.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v4p50/r7.claim: Qatadah glosses the phrase as 'adorned it for him.'
THALABI:v4p50/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد: شجعت. قتادة: زينت. فقتله

THALABI:v4p50/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p50/r8.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v4p50/r8.claim: Al-Suddi says Cain evaded Abel in the mountains, then found him asleep while tending sheep and smashed his head with a rock.
THALABI:v4p50/r8.anchor: قال السدي: فلما أراد قتل هابيل راغ الغلام في رؤوس الجبال.

THALABI:v4p50/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p50/r9.speaker: ابن جريح
THALABI:v4p50/r9.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Cain did not know how to kill; Iblis demonstrated by crushing a bird's head between stones, and Cain copied him. Abel was twenty; accounts differ about where he died.
THALABI:v4p50/r9.anchor: وقال ابن جريح: لم يدر قابيل كيف يقتل هابيل، فتمثل له إبليس وأخذ طيرا

THALABI:v4p50/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p50/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p50/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas locates Abel's killing on Mount Nawd.
THALABI:v4p50/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس: على جبل نود، وقال بعضهم: عند عقبة حرا

THALABI:v4p50/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p50/r11.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v4p50/r11.claim: Another account places the killing near the pass of Hira.
THALABI:v4p50/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس: على جبل نود، وقال بعضهم: عند عقبة حرا

THALABI:v4p50/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p50/r12.speaker: جعفر الصادق
THALABI:v4p50/r12.claim: Jaʿfar al-Sadiq locates the killing at the site of the Great Mosque in Basra.
THALABI:v4p50/r12.anchor: حكى محمد بن جرير، وقال جعفر الصادق: بالبصرة في موضع المسجد الأعظم

THALABI:v4p51/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p51/r1.speaker: الأوزاعي
THALABI:v4p51/r1.claim: Al-Awzaʿi reports from al-Muttalib ibn ʿAbd Allah that the earth shook for seven days after Abel's murder, drank his blood, and was forbidden ever to drink blood again; God confronted Cain over the blood crying from the ground.
THALABI:v4p51/r1.anchor: يدل عليه ما أخبر الأوزاعي عن المطلب بن عبد الله المخزومي قال: لما قتل ابن آدم أخاه

THALABI:v4p51/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p51/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p51/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says that while Adam was in Mecca, Cain's murder made trees uproot, foods change, fruit sour, water bitter, and the earth dusty; Adam sensed an event and found Abel dead in India.
THALABI:v4p51/r2.anchor: مقاتل بن الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال: لما قتل قابيل هابيل وآدم بمكة اشتال الشجر

THALABI:v4p51/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p51/r3.speaker: آدم
THALABI:v4p51/r3.claim: The account attributes to Adam an elegy for Abel, beginning with the changed land and its dust-covered face.
THALABI:v4p51/r3.anchor: فأنشأ يقول، وهو أول من قال الشعر: تغيرت البلاد ومن عليها

THALABI:v4p51/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p51/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p51/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, as transmitted by Maymun ibn Mihran, rejects the claim that Adam composed Arabic poetry, saying it falsely accuses Adam and citing 36:69 that Muhammad was not taught poetry.
THALABI:v4p51/r4.anchor: وروى ميمون بن مهران عن ابن عباس قال: من قال إن آدم قال شعرا فقد كذب على الله ورسوله

THALABI:v4p51/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p51/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p51/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reconciles the elegy by saying Adam lamented in Syriac, not Arabic poetry; he entrusted it to Seth, and it passed to Yaʿrub ibn Qahtan, who reordered it into meter without adding or removing a letter and was the first to write Arabic.
THALABI:v4p51/r5.anchor: إن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم والأنبياء كلهم صلوات الله عليهم في النهي عن الشعر سواء، قال الله تعالى

THALABI:v4p52/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p52/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p52/r1.claim: The continued elegy mourns Abel's death, the burial that holds him, and Adam's grief and weariness with life after losing his son.
THALABI:v4p52/r1.anchor: ل فوا حزني لقد فقد المليح

THALABI:v4p52/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p52/r2.speaker: إبليس
THALABI:v4p52/r2.claim: Iblis answers Adam's lament with a taunting poem, telling him to leave the land and blaming his loss of Paradise on Iblis's schemes.
THALABI:v4p52/r2.anchor: فأجابه إبليس في جوف الليل شامتا: تنح عن البلاد وساكنيها

THALABI:v4p52/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p52/r3.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
THALABI:v4p52/r3.claim: Salim ibn Abi al-Jaʿd says Adam mourned for a hundred years; at age 130, five years after Abel's murder, Eve bore Seth, whose name means God's gift and who replaced Abel.
THALABI:v4p52/r3.anchor: وقال سالم بن أبي الجعد: لما قتل هابيل مكث آدم (عليه السلام) مائة سنة لا أكثر

THALABI:v4p52/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p52/r4.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
THALABI:v4p52/r4.claim: In the same account, God taught Seth the hours of night and day and the worship performed in each, and made him Adam's successor.
THALABI:v4p52/r4.anchor: وقال سالم بن أبي الجعد: لما قتل هابيل مكث آدم (عليه السلام) مائة سنة لا أكثر. ثم أتى فقيل: حياك الله

THALABI:v4p52/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p52/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p52/r5.claim: Cain was ordered to go as a fugitive and wanderer, afraid and shunned; he took his sister Hibatu Allah to Aden in Yemen.
THALABI:v4p52/r5.anchor: وأما قابيل فقيل له: اذهب طريدا شريدا فزعا مرهوبا لا يأمن من يراه

THALABI:v4p52/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p52/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p52/r6.claim: Iblis deceived Cain into thinking fire had consumed Abel's offering because Abel worshipped fire; Cain then established fire worship for his descendants, becoming the first to do so.
THALABI:v4p52/r6.anchor: فأتاه إبليس، فقال له: إنما أكلت النار قربان هابيل لأنه كان يعبد النار

THALABI:v4p52/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p52/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p52/r7.claim: A final report says Cain threw stones at passersby; a blind grandson accidentally killed Cain with a stone, then his son accused him, and the blind man killed that son with a slap.
THALABI:v4p52/r7.anchor: قالوا: كان لا يمر به أحدا من ولده إلا رماه، فأقبل ابن لقابيل أعمى ومعه ابن له

THALABI:v4p53/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p53/r1.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v4p53/r1.claim: Mujahid says Cain’s leg was fastened to his thigh and shin until resurrection, while his face turned with the sun between a summer fire enclosure and winter snow.
THALABI:v4p53/r1.anchor: قال مجاهد: فعلقت إحدى رجل قابيل إلى فخذه وساقه وعلقت يومئذ إلى يوم القيامة

THALABI:v4p53/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p53/r2.speaker: قالوا
THALABI:v4p53/r2.claim: Cain’s descendants adopted musical instruments and gave themselves over to amusement, wine, fire worship, adultery, and other indecencies; God’s flood in Noah’s time destroyed them, leaving Seth’s line.
THALABI:v4p53/r2.anchor: قالوا: واتخذ أولاد قابيل آلات اللهو من اليراع والطنبور، والمزامير، والعيدان

THALABI:v4p53/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p53/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
THALABI:v4p53/r3.claim: Ibn Umar says the first killer receives exactly half the punishment of the people of Hell.
THALABI:v4p53/r3.anchor: قال عبد الله بن عمر: إنا لنجد ابن آدم القاتل يقاسم أهل النار العذاب قسمة صحيحة

THALABI:v4p53/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p53/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v4p53/r4.claim: The Prophet says every Muslim killed unjustly leaves a share of that bloodguilt on Adam’s first son because he instituted murder.
THALABI:v4p53/r4.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «لا تقتل نفس مسلمة ظلما إلا كان على ابن آدم [الأول] كفل من دمه

THALABI:v4p53/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p53/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v4p53/r5.claim: In a report from Anas, the Prophet calls Tuesday a day of blood because Eve menstruated and Adam’s son killed his brother that day.
THALABI:v4p53/r5.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن يوم الثلاثاء فقال: «يوم دم»

THALABI:v4p53/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p53/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v4p53/r6.claim: Anas reports that God bestowed three benefits: wind after life so relatives bury their dead, worms in grain so rulers do not hoard it as money, and death after old age eases weariness for the old and their family.
THALABI:v4p53/r6.anchor: عن أنس قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «امتن الله عز وجل على ابن آدم بثلاث بعد ثلاث، بالريح بعد الروح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r1.claim: Al-Farra glosses the phrase as the soul following and complying with him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r2.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad analyzes ṭawwaʿat as a verb derived from ṭawʿ, willing obedience.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r3.claim: Mujahid glosses the soul as emboldening him; Abu Ubayd explains that it assisted him and answered his wish, deriving the sense from compliance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: {فطوعت له نفسه} قال: شجعته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r4.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r4.claim: Al-Azhari considers the likeliest sense to be that the soul made killing his brother easy and tolerable.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r4.anchor: قال الأزهري: والأشبه عندي أن يكون معنى: (طوعت) سمحت وسهلت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r5.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r5.claim: On al-Azhari's reading, qatla is accusative directly: the soul portrayed the killing as easy, without an elided preposition.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r5.anchor: فينتصب القتل على هذا من غير إضمار ولا حذف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r6.speaker: الزجاجي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaji likewise selects making the act easy, deriving ṭawwaʿa from ṭāʿa, to become easy and compliant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r6.anchor: واختار الزجاجي هذا الوجه فقال: طوع فعل من طاع الشيء يطوع إذا سهل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r7.speaker: الفراء والمبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r7.claim: On al-Farra and al-Mubarrad's analysis, qatla is accusative after deleting a preposition, as if the soul complied with killing his brother.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r7.anchor: وأما قول (¬5) الفراء والمبرد فانتصاب قوله: {قتل أخيه}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Ata's report, says his soul enticed him to kill his brother.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r8.anchor: فقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: فسولت له نفسه قتل أخيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r9.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r9.claim: Qatada says his soul adorned the killing for him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r10.speaker: يمان
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r10.claim: Yaman says his soul made the killing easy for him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r11.speaker: عبد العزيز بن يحيى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r11.claim: Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya says his soul consented to the killing.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r11.anchor: وقال عبد العزيز بن يحيى (¬4): أجابته إلى ذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r12.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r12.claim: Al-Kalbi says his soul complied with him in killing his brother.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p340#2/r12.anchor: وقال الكلبي: تابعته نفسه على قتل أخيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p342/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p342/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p342/r1.claim: Exegetes say Cain did not know how to kill; Satan showed him by crushing a bird's head between stones, and Cain later killed sleeping Habil by smashing his head with a stone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p342/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون: لم يدر قابيل كيف يقتل هابيل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p342/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p342/r2.speaker: عبد الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p342/r2.claim: The Prophet said that for every unjust killing a share of bloodguilt falls on Adam's son, since he was the first to institute murder; Masruq transmits this from Abd Allah.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p342/r2.anchor: وروى مسروق عن عبد الله (¬8) عن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p342/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p342/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p342/r3.claim: Ali identifies the two who ask to see the ones who led them astray in 41:29 as Iblis and Adam's son who killed his brother, the first to commit disobedience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p342/r3.anchor: فقال علي: هو إبليس وابن آدم الذي قتل أخاه، كانا أول من عمل بالمعصية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p342/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p342/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p342/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says Cain lost both worlds: he angered his parents and was left without a brother, and angered his Lord and went to Hell.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p342/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد خسر دنياه وآخرته، أما الدنيا فأسخط والديه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p342/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p342/r5.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p342/r5.claim: Exegetes say Cain fled to Aden in Yemen; Satan falsely told him fire had accepted Habil's offering because Habil served it, so Cain built a fire temple for himself and descendants and became the first fire worshipper.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v7p342/r5.anchor: قال المفسرون: إن قابيل لما قتل أخاه هرب إلى عدن من أرض اليمن

QASHANI:5:30-31/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:30-31/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:30-31/r1.claim: The soul makes murder easy by persuading estimation to stop intellect's proper activity and veil it from guidance.
QASHANI:5:30-31/r1.anchor: بمنعه عن أفعاله الخاصة وحجبه عن نور الهداية

QASHANI:5:30-31/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:30-31/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:30-31/r2.claim: Estimation's victory harms the soul by replacing intellect's guidance and sound judgment with its own error; unsupported by reason, it stirs damaging appetites and excess.
QASHANI:5:30-31/r2.anchor: لتضرره باستيلائه على العقل واستبدال ضلالته وخطئه بهداية العقل وصوابه

QASHANI:5:30-31/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:5:30-31/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:5:30-31/r3.claim: Unrestrained estimation incites greedy pursuit of wealth and rank and animal pleasures; excess can weaken or destroy estimation itself.
QASHANI:5:30-31/r3.anchor: مثل شدة الحرص في طلب المال والجاه والإفراط فيضعف الوهم أيضا أو يبطل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r7.claim: His soul made the murder easy and adorned it; he lost this world by angering his parents and the next by God's wrath.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r7.anchor: { فطوعت له نفسه قتل أخيه } سهلته وزينت له ذلك { فقتله فأصبح من الخاسرين } خسر دنياه بإسخاط والديه، وآخرته بسخط الله عليه،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r8.claim: Cain did not know what to do with the first human corpse among Adam's descendants, so he carried it in a sack on his back.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:5:27-30/r8.anchor: فلما قتله لم يدر ما يصنع به؛ لأنه كان أول ميت على وجه الأرض من بني آدم، فحمله في جراب على ظهره.

ELMALILI:5:27-31/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r20.claim: The wrongdoer’s soul made fratricide seem easy, unobstructed, and appealing, even as if it were an obedient act; it eased and encouraged the crime.
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r20.anchor: böyle büyük bir cinayeti güya bir tâat sevkiyle endişesiz yapılabilecek, mâni‘den âzâde

ELMALILI:5:27-31/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r21.claim: Taṭwīʿ here is the causative form of ṭawʿ, expressing that the soul rendered the murder compliant and easy for him.

ELMALILI:5:27-31/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r22.claim: The idiom “the pasture was spread for him” means there was plenty before him to graze as he wished; here murder was presented like a ready pasture.
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r22.anchor: طاَعَ لَهُ الْمَرْتَعُ derler ki “istediği gibi otlamak için otlak önüne bol bol seriliverdi” demektir

ELMALILI:5:27-31/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r23.claim: He killed his brother and became one of the losers, gaining no benefit and suffering loss in both religion and worldly life.
ELMALILI:5:27-31/r23.anchor: kendisine bir fâide temin etmek ihtimâli olmadıktan başka dininde de dünyasında da ziyan etti

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:29/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:29/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:29/r6.claim: The brother’s advice briefly made the killer hesitate, but his jealousy overwhelmed it; his own soul drove him to murder, after which he became a loser in this life and the next and opened a precedent whose later murderers’ guilt he shares.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:29/r6.anchor: Nefsi onu kardeşini öldürmek gibi korkunç bir cinayete itmiş ve bundan başka hiçbir şey onun nefsânî duygularını tatmin etmemiştir. Sonuçta kardeşini öl

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:29/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:29/r7.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:29/r7.claim: The Prophet says every person unjustly killed leaves a share of that bloodshed for Adam’s first son, because he was the first murderer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:29/r7.anchor: Hz. Peygamber bir hadisinde şöyle buyurmaktadır: “Haksız yere öldürülen hiçbir kimse yoktur ki onun kanından Âdem’in ilk oğluna bir pay ayrılmasın.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:29/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:29/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:29/r8.claim: The story implies that Adam’s children believed in God, the afterlife, reckoning, punishment, and Hell, and understood piety, fear of God, and worship through sacrifice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:5:29/r8.anchor: Kıssadan Hz. Âdem’in çocuklarının Allah’a, âhirete, hesaba, cezaya ve cehenneme inandıkları; Allah korkusu ve takvâ gibi konularda bilinç sahip oldukları

QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r1.claim: The soul’s intrusive promptings gain control only after divine admonitions are veiled and repeated corrupt intentions bury the calls of truth.
QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r1.anchor: لا تستولي هواجس النفوس على صاحبها إلا بعد استتار مواعظ الحق

QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r2.claim: The soul is naturally drawn to appetite and disobedience; following it soon brings regret, which then cannot repair the harm.
QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r2.anchor: والنفس لا تدعو إلا إلى اتباع الشهوات ومتابعة المعصية

QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r3.claim: God intends people to take prudent care in livelihood and supplies a means of recognition when a subtle practical solution is unclear.
QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r3.anchor: إرادة الحق - سبحانه - وصول الخلق إلى لطف الاحتياط في أسباب التعيش

QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r4.speaker: النبي
QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r4.claim: The Prophet says that whoever inaugurates a good or bad practice receives its own reward or burden and that of those who follow it until the Resurrection.
QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r4.anchor: من سن حسنة فله أجرها وأجر من عمل بها إلى يوم والقيامة

QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r5.claim: Corruption has outward forms, punished through the rulings of jurisprudence, and inward forms, whose punishment reaches a person’s spiritual secrets.
QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r5.anchor: السعي في الفساد على ضربين : بالظاهر وعقوبته معلومة في مسائل الفقه

QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r6.claim: Inward punishment severs divine inspirations and brings eclipse of gnosis, veiling after unveiling, estrangement after intimacy, loss of enabling grace, and exclusion from worship into following the lower soul.
QUSHAYRI:v1p261/r6.anchor: وذلك بقطع ما كان متصلا من واردات الحق ، وكسوف شمس العرفان ، والستر بعد الكشف

AKHFASH:v1p279/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p279/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p279/r3.claim: Ṭawwaʿat means made easy or permissible; ṭawwaqtuhu amrī means I bound him to my affair.

FARRA:v1p304/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p304/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p304/r7.claim: Fa-ṭawwaʿat lahu nafsuhu means his soul yielded to him or followed him toward killing his brother.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p142#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p142#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p142#6/r1.claim: His soul made the killing easy for him, cooperating and yielding to the act.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p142#6/r1.anchor: {فطوعت له نفسه} أي: شايعته (3) وانقادت له.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p142#6/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p142#6/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p142#6/r2.claim: The form is from ṭāʿa, to comply; had it come from aṭāʿa, the forms would be muṭīʿ, ṭāʿa, and iṭāʿa.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p142#6/r2.anchor: ولو كان من أطاع لكان مطيعا وطاعة وإطاعة.

MAJAZ:v1p160/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p160/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p160/r5.claim: His soul made the killing seem easy, encouraged him, and obeyed him; ṭāʿat lahu means it obeyed him.
MAJAZ:v1p160/r5.anchor: «فطوعت له نفسه» (30) أي شجعته وآتته على قتله، وطاعت له، أي أطاعته

NAHHAS:v2p16/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p16/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر
NAHHAS:v2p16/r7.claim: Abu Jaʿfar calls the preceding explanation far-fetched, since ordinary Arabic says ‘his soul complied with him.’
NAHHAS:v2p16/r7.anchor: قال أبو جعفر هذا بعيد لأنه إنما يقال طاوعته نفسه

NAHHAS:v2p16/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p16/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p16/r8.claim: The soul made the killing desirable to him.
NAHHAS:v2p16/r8.anchor: أي أحدث له شهوة في هذا

SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r1.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r1.claim: The majority read ṭawwaʿat with a doubled wāw and no alif.
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r1.anchor: الجمهور على " طوعت " مشدد الواو من غير ألف

SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r2.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r2.claim: This reading means that the soul made the killing easy or prompted it.

SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī derives the sense “made spacious and easy” from ṭāʿa lahu al-martaʿ, when pasture expands.
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r3.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " وسعته ويسرته من " طاع له المرتع " إذا اتسع

SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r4.claim: Al-Samīn analyzes the doubled form as causative: killing initially yielded to the soul, and the doubled verb makes it an object, as with the hamza form.
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r4.anchor: والتضعيف فيه للتعدية لأن الأصل: طاع له قتل أخيه

SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r5.speaker: الحسن وزيد بن علي
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, and many others read ṭāwaʿat with an alif.
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r5.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وزيد بن علي وجماعة كثيرة: " فطاوعت "

SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows form III to mean form I without mutual action, citing paired examples; Sībawayh discusses this pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r6.anchor: الزمخشري فيها احتمالين، أحدهما: أن يكون مما جاء فيه فاعل

SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r7.claim: Alternatively, he takes the form as reciprocal: killing called the soul to act, while the soul recoiled until killing overcame it and it yielded.
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r7.anchor: جعل القتل يدعو إلى نفسه لأجل الحسد الذي لحق قابيل

SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r8.claim: The phrase lahu attaches to ṭawwaʿat on either reading.
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r8.anchor: " له " متعلق ب " طوعت " على القراءتين

SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls lahu an added connective: the clause would be complete without it, as in “I guarded Zayd’s property.”
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r9.anchor: قال الزمخشري: و " له " لزيادة الربط

SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r10.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r10.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ rejects direct transitivity without the lām here, since that construction takes one object while the verse already has “the killing of his brother.”
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r10.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء " وقال قوم: طاوعت تتعدى بغير لام

SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r11.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r11.claim: He also gives an alternative underlying construction: “his soul complied with him regarding the killing,” with the lām replacing omitted ʿalā.
SAMIN-DURR:5:30/r11.anchor: وقيل: التقدير: طاوعته نفسه على قتل أخيه، فزاد اللام وحذف " على "

ZAJJAJ:v2p167/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p167/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p167/r1.claim: The phrase means that his soul complied with the killing of his brother.

ZAJJAJ:v2p167/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p167/r2.speaker: أبو العباس محمد بن يزيد المبرد
ZAJJAJ:v2p167/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad explains the phrase as فغلت from الطوع, voluntary compliance.
ZAJJAJ:v2p167/r2.anchor: وقال أبو العباس محمد بن يزيد المبرد: (فطوعت له نفسه)

ZAJJAJ:v2p167/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p167/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p167/r3.claim: Arab usage طاع له means that something came to him willingly, as in the examples of branches coming within reach and an offered thing.
ZAJJAJ:v2p167/r3.anchor: والعرب تقول: طاع لهذه الظبية أصول هذه الشجرة، وطاع له كذا وكذا، أي أتاه طوعا.

ZAJJAJ:v2p167/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p167/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p167/r4.claim: He became one of those who lost their good deeds.

ZAJJAJ:v2p167/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p167/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p167/r5.claim: After killing his brother, Cain stripped off his clothes and left him naked in a desolate plain.
ZAJJAJ:v2p167/r5.anchor: وكان حين قتله سلبه ثيابه وتركه عاريا بالأرض القفار.

ASAD-NOTES:5:30#n37/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:5:30#n37/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:5:30#n37/r1.claim: Although nafs can mean soul, mind, or self, Asad reads it here as desire or passionate determination and prefers “passion,” citing Qamus and Zamakhshari’s Asas.
ASAD-NOTES:5:30#n37/r1.anchor: Among the many meanings attributable to the noun nafs (primarily, "soul", or "mind", or "self"), there is also that of "desire" or "passionate determination"

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1046/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1046/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1046/r1.claim: “سولت” means the self embellished and eased an act; “طوعت” is stronger, requiring effort to train the self. Cain had to overcome resistance to killing his brother, unlike the easier acts of the Samiri and Joseph’s brothers; the Quran’s terms are not interchangeable.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1046/r1.anchor: فيها جهد ومبالغة في التطويع حتى تروضه وتذلله

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p209/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p209/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p209/r1.claim: Al-Hasan ibn ʿImran, Abu Waqid, and al-Jarrah read فطاوعت; Ibn Jinnī says the urge to kill drew Cain toward it, and his soul answered and cooperated.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p209/r1.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة الحسن بن عمران وأبي واقد والجراح، ورويت عن الحسن:

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p209/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p209/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p209/r2.claim: The common reading means that Cain’s soul made killing his brother seem good and easy to him.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p209/r2.anchor: وقراءة العامة: {فطوعت له} أي: حسنته له وسهلته عليه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r1.speaker: النبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r1.claim: The Prophet says every unjust killing adds a share of its bloodguilt to Adam’s first son, because he established the practice of murder.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r1.anchor: بقول صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لا تقتل نفس ظلما إلا كان على ابن آدم الأول كفل من دمها، لأنه أول من سن القتل»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Cain’s soul impelled him to kill.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس: بعثته على قتله.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r12.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid explain the phrase as encouragement to kill.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس: بعثته على قتله. وقال أيضا هو ومجاهد: شجعته.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r13.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r13.claim: Qatāda says the soul made the murder seem attractive.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r14.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r14.claim: Al-Akhfash explains the phrase as the soul permitting the murder.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r15.speaker: المبرد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r15.claim: Al-Mubarrad derives the expression from ṭawʿ, citing the Arab idiom ṭāʿa lahu kadhā for something that came willingly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r15.anchor: وقال المبرد: من الطوع، والعرب تقول: طاع له كذا أي أتاه طوعا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r16.speaker: ابن قتيبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r16.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the soul accompanied him and submitted to the act.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r16.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: تابعته وانقادت له.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r17.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r17.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī glosses the phrase as making the murder spacious and easy for him, from the usage of pasture spreading out.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r17.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وسعته له ويسرته، من طاع له المرتع إذا اتسع.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r18.claim: These close explanations derive from submission: murder was intrinsically difficult, but the insistent soul made it yield and become easy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p231/r18.anchor: وهذه أقوال متقاربة في المعنى، وهو فعل من الطوع وهو الانقياد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r1.claim: The root construction ṭāʿa lahu qatl akhīhi means the murder yielded and became easy; causative gemination makes the killing the object, portraying the soul’s submission to an otherwise grave act.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r1.anchor: طاع له قتل أخيه أي انقاد له وسهل، ثم عدي بالتضعيف فصار الفاعل مفعولا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r2.speaker: الحسن وزيد بن علي والجراح والحسن بن عمران وأبو واقد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Jarrāḥ, al-Ḥasan ibn ʿImrān and Abū Wāqid read fa-ṭāwaʿat, suggesting mutual interaction between the murder and the soul.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وزيد بن علي والجراح، والحسن بن عمران، وأبو واقد: فطاوعته،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r3.claim: For fa-ṭāwaʿat, al-Zamakhsharī offers either form III with form-I meaning, or the murder calling the soul to act while it does not resist.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فيه وجهان: أن يكون مما جاء من فاعل بمعنى فعل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān accepts al-Zamakhsharī’s second explanation: the murder called the soul to proceed and it complied.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r4.anchor: فأما الوجه الثاني فهو موافق لما ذكرناه، وأما الوجه الأول فقد ذكر سيبويه:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r5.claim: Sībawayh allows fāʿala without two agents, citing ḍāʿaftu/ḍaʿaftu and nāʿamtu/naʿimtu; Abū Ḥayyān faults Ibn ʿAṣfūr and Ibn Mālik for omitting this pattern.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r5.anchor: فقد ذكر سيبويه: ضاعفت وضعفت مثل: ناعمت ونعمت.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r6.claim: The added lahu strengthens the connection in the sentence; fatuwwiʿat nafsuhu qatl akhīhi would already be complete without it, like ḥafiẓtu māla Zayd.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r6.anchor: يعني: أنه لو جاء فطوعت نفسه قتل أخيه لكان كلاما تاما جاريا على كلام العرب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r7.claim: Commentators dispute the manner and place of the killing and Cain’s age, but the verse itself gives none of those details.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r7.anchor: وتكلم المفسرون في أشياء من كيفيته، ومكان قتله، وعمره حين قتل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r8.anchor: أصبح من الخاسرين أصبح: بمعنى صار. وقال ابن عطية:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says a part of time stands for the whole and morning is used because it begins the day and suggests activity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: أقيم بعض الزمان مقام كله، وخص الصباح بذلك لأنه بدء النهار والانبعاث

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r10.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s explanation: aṣbaḥa, like aḍḥā, ẓalla, amsā and bāta, became a general verb meaning ṣāra, not because morning begins the day.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r10.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكره من تعليل كون أصبح عبارة عن جميع أوقاته، وأقيم بعض الزمان مقام كله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Cain lost in this life by angering his parents and becoming brotherless, and in the next by angering God and entering Hell.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس: خسر في الدنيا بإسخاط والديه وبقائه بغير أخ، وفي الآخرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r12.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r12.claim: Al-Zajjāj glosses the losers as those who lost their good deeds.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r13.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r13.claim: Qāḍī Abū Yaʿlā says Cain lost himself by destroying it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r13.anchor: وقال القاضي أبو يعلى: من الخاسرين أنفسهم بإهلاكهم إياها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r14.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r14.claim: Mujāhid describes Cain’s punishment as a leg bound to his thigh until Judgment, facing the sun, with an enclosure of fire in summer and snow in winter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p232/r14.anchor: قال مجاهد: خسرانه أن علقت إحدى رجلي القاتل لساقها إلى فخذها من يومئذ إلى يوم القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r1.claim: Fatawwaʿat means that his soul made the killing easy for him and widened its scope; the root can describe spacious pasture.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r1.anchor: فسهلته له ووسعته من طاع له المرتع إذا اتسع

ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r2.claim: Placing the soul's persuasion after Habil's speech reflects either a new act of resolve after resistance or Qabil's confidence once he saw Habil would not defend himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r2.anchor: لما أن بقاء الفعل بعد تقرر مايزيله وإن كان استمرارا عليه بحسب الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r3.claim: Calling Habil his brother heightens the condemnation of what Qabil's soul urged him to do.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r3.anchor: والتصريح بأخوته لكمال تقبيح ماسولته نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r4.claim: Al-Hasan reads faṭāwaʿat instead of the canonical faṭawwaʿat.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن فطاوعت وفيها وجهان : الأول أن فاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r5.claim: One explanation of al-Hasan's form treats Form III as equivalent to Form II, a usage also found by Sibawayh and others and close to the canonical reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r5.anchor: الأول أن فاعل بمعنى فعل كما ذكره سيبويه وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, the reciprocal form is metaphorical: murder urges the soul, the soul resists, and in the end the soul yields to the stronger urge to kill.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r6.anchor: والثانى أن المفاعلة مجازية بجعل القتل يدعو النفس إلى الإقدام عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r7.claim: The pronoun li-hu adds emphasis and clarification, as in 94:1; the suggestion that it excludes someone else persuading him is unsound.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r7.anchor: للتأكيد والتبيين كما فى قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد وابن جريج
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r8.claim: A report says Qabil did not know how to kill; Iblis appeared as a bird and taught him by crushing another bird's head between two stones, after which Qabil killed his surrendered brother.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r8.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير عن ابن مجاهد وابن جريج أن قابيل لم يدر كيف يقتل هابيل

ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r9.claim: Another account says Qabil searched the mountains, then found Habil asleep while tending sheep and killed him with a rock, leaving the body exposed because he did not know how to bury it.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r9.anchor: وأخرج عن ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة رضى الله تعالى عنهم أن قابيل طلب أخاه

ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r10.speaker: عمرو الشبعانى عن كعب الأخبار
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r10.claim: Kaʿb al-Ahbar is reported by ʿAmr al-Shaʿbani to have located the killing on Mount Dayr al-Murran, with another report placing it on Mount Qasiyun.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r10.anchor: فعن عمرو الشبعانى عن كعب الأخبار أنه قتل على جبل دير المران

ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r11.claim: Other locations given are near the pass of Hira or at Basra, where the great mosque stands.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r11.anchor: وقيل : عند عقبة حراء وقيل بالبصرة فى موضع المسجد الأعظم

ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r12.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن فضالة
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r12.claim: A report from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Fadala says God altered Qabil's mind and removed his heart after the murder, leaving him a wanderer until death.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r12.anchor: أخرج نعيم بن حماد عن عبد الرحمن بن فضالة أنه لما قتل قابيل هابيل

ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r13.claim: An account says Qabil's formerly white body turned black after he killed Habil; Adam questioned him and attributed the change to his crime.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r13.anchor: وروى أنه لما قتله اسود جسده وكان أبيض فسأله آدم عن أخيه

ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r14.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r14.claim: Salim ibn Abi al-Jaʿd reports that Adam mourned his murdered son without laughing for a hundred years, then rejoiced when told he would have a son.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r14.anchor: عن سالم بن أبى الجعد قال : إن آدم عليه السلام لما قتل أحد بنيه

ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r15.speaker: محيى السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r15.claim: Muhyi al-Sunna says Seth was born fifty years after the murder, his name means God's gift and he replaced Habil; God taught him the hours and worship practices, sent him fifty scriptures, and made him Adam's heir.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r15.anchor: وذكر محيى السنة أنه عليه السلام ولد له بعد قتل ولده بخمسين سنة شيت

ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r16.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r16.claim: Ibn Jarir reports from Ali that Adam mourned Habil in verse; al-Khatib and Ibn ʿAsakir transmit a similar report from Ibn ʿAbbas, which became famous.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p114#2/r16.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن على كرم الله تعالى وجهه قال : لما قتل ابن آدم عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r1.speaker: ميمون بن مهران عن الحبر
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r1.claim: Maimun ibn Mihran transmits Ibn ʿAbbas's denial that Adam composed poetry, since Muhammad and all prophets were equally forbidden to do so; he says Adam's Syriac elegy was later rearranged into Arabic verse by Yarub.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r1.anchor: وروى عن ميمون بن مهران عن الحبر رضى الله تعالى عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r2.claim: Some Arabic scholars found grammatical defects, imperfect rhyme, or forced poetic license in the attributed lines; the author says they should not even be attributed to Yarub because of their evident weakness.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r2.anchor: وذكر بعض علماء العربية إن فى ذلك الشعر لحنا أو إقواءا

ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r3.claim: Qabil became a loser in this world and the next.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r3.anchor: دنيا وآخرة أخرج الشيخان وغيرهما عن ابن مسعود

ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r4.claim: The Prophet says that every unjustly killed person leaves a share of the bloodguilt on Adam's first son because he instituted murder.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r4.anchor: أخرج الشيخان وغيرهما عن ابن مسعود رضى الله تعالى عنه قال : قال رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the first killer shares Hell's punishment with its inhabitants and bears half their punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r5.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال : إنا لنجد ابن آدم القاتل

ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r6.claim: The cited reports, including a report that Qabil was one of the wretched, indicate that he died an unbeliever.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r6.anchor: وهذا ونحوه صريح فى أن الرجل مات كافرا

ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r7.claim: A report says Qabil fled to Aden, where Iblis persuaded him to worship fire as the reason Habil's offering had been accepted; Qabil built a fire temple and became the first fire-worshipper.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r7.anchor: فأتاه إبليس عليهما اللعنة فقال : إنما أكلت النار قربان هابيل

ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r8.claim: Al-Alusi says Qabil likely bears the burden of later fire-worship and perhaps of everyone who worships something other than God.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r8.anchor: والظاهر أن عليه أيضا وزر من يعبد النار بل لايعبد أن يكون عليه وزر

ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r9.claim: Asbaha does not prove the killing happened at night; Arabs use it for coming into a state of loss regardless of time.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r9.anchor: فان من عادة العرب أن يقولوا : أصبح فلان خسار الصفقة

ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r10.claim: The wording became one of the losers, rather than simply a loser, intensifies the claim even though no one else had yet lost as he did.
ALUSI-FULL:v6p115/r10.anchor: وإنما لم يقل سبحانه فأصبح خاسرا للمبالغة وإن لم يكن حينئذ

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r1.claim: The soul complied with, accompanied, and helped him in the killing of his brother.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r1.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {فطوعت له نفسه} أي: طاوعته وشايعته وعاونته، {قتل أخيه}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r2.claim: قتل أخيه is understood as “in the killing of his brother.”

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r3.claim: Mujahid glosses the soul’s action as encouraging Cain.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r4.claim: Qatada says Cain’s soul made the murder seem attractive to him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: فزينت له نفسه، وقال يمان:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r5.speaker: يمان
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r5.claim: Yaman says Cain’s soul made the act easy for him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r5.anchor: وقال يمان: سهلت له نفسه ذلك، أي: جعلته سهلا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r6.claim: The soul portrayed the killing to Cain as an easy act he could readily undertake.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r6.anchor: تقديره: صورت له نفسه أن قتل أخيه طوع له أي سهل عليه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r7.claim: Ibn Jurayj relates that Iblis showed Cain how to kill by smashing a bird’s head between stones; Cain watched and imitated him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن جريج: فتمثل له إبليس وأخذ طيرا فوضع رأسه على حجر ثم شدخ رأسه بحجر آخر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r8.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r8.claim: One account says Abel was killed while submitting.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r8.anchor: قيل: قتل وهو مستسلم، وقيل: اغتاله وهو

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r9.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r9.claim: Another account says Cain attacked Abel while he slept and smashed his head.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: اغتاله وهو في النوم فشدخ رأسه فقتله،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r10.claim: Abel was twenty years old when he was killed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r10.anchor: وكان لهابيل يوم قتل عشرون سنة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r11.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r11.claim: One location account places the killing at Basra, at the great mosque site, and says Cain’s body blackened; Adam confronted him and then did not laugh for a hundred years.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r11.anchor: واختلفوا في موضع قتله [قيل: بالبصرة في موضع المسجد الأعظم فاسود جسم القاتل وسأله آدم عليه السلام عن أخيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas places the killing on Mount Thawr.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: على جبل [ثور]

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r13.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r13.claim: Another location given is near Aqabat Hira.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p43#2/r13.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: على جبل [ثور] (3) وقيل عند عقبة حراء،

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:30/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:30/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:30/r5.claim: His soul made the killing easy and widened it for him, as pasture is said to be spacious.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:30/r5.anchor: فسهلته له ووسعته من طاع له المرتع إذا اتسع

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:30/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:30/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:30/r6.claim: The variant faṭāwaʿat may be an active form equivalent in meaning to faʿala, or it may picture the killing inviting him and him complying.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:30/r6.anchor: وقرىء «فطاوعت» على أنه فاعل بمعنى فعل

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:30/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:30/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:30/r7.claim: The lām is an added connective, as in “I preserved Zayd his property.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:30/r7.anchor: وله لزيادة الربط كقولك حفظت لزيد ماله

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:30/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:30/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:30/r8.claim: He lost both religion and worldly life, remaining exiled and grief-stricken for the rest of his life.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:30/r8.anchor: دينا ودنيا، إذ بقي مدة عمره مطرودا محزونا

BAYDAWI-FULL:5:30/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:30/r9.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:30/r9.claim: Reports place Abel’s death at age twenty near Ḥirāʾ, or in Basra at the site of the Great Mosque.
BAYDAWI-FULL:5:30/r9.anchor: قيل قتل هابيل وهو ابن عشرين سنة عند عقبة حراء. وقيل: بالبصرة في موضع المسجد الأعظم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r1.claim: Although Abel’s warning should have led Cain to obey and avoid sin, Cain’s hardened heart instead turns it into a motive for murder.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r1.anchor: هذا الوعظ جديرا بأن يكون سببا لطاعته وزاجرا له عن معصيته

BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r2.claim: The intensive form signals that the sanctity and awe of murder made Cain’s soul require a strenuous process to make the act seem easy.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r2.anchor: إذ القتل لما جعل الله له من الحرمة وكساه من الهيبة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r3.claim: Cain’s soul treated him with specious rationalizations, emboldened him, and overcame his reason; one who imagines a sin’s punishment normally resists it, but a dominated person yields to his soul.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r3.anchor: حتى غلبت على عقله فانطاع لها وانقاد فأقدم عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r4.claim: The killing follows from the soul’s enticement, and loss follows from the murder.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r5.claim: Morning is named because it is a time when relief is expected, but becoming a loser describes Cain at every time.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r6.claim: Cain loses through God’s anger at his assault on God’s creation and through the anger of his fellow humans at his attack on one of their kind.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r6.anchor: وغضب أبناء جنسه عليه لاجترائه على أحدهم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r7.speaker: قيل
BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r7.claim: A report says Cain did not know how to kill; Satan demonstrated by smashing a bird’s head with a stone, and Cain copied him while Abel slept.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p447/r7.anchor: قيل : إنه لم يدر كيف يقتله

DURR-FULL:v3p60/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r1.claim: The Prophet urged a man facing a would-be killer to act like the better of Adam’s two sons; the victim is in Paradise and his killer in Hell.
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي شيبة عن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يعجز أحدكم أتاه الرجل أن يقتله أن يقول هكذا

DURR-FULL:v3p60/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r2.claim: Qatada glosses the phrase as the killer’s soul embellishing the murder for him.
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {فطوعت له نفسه قتل أخيه}

DURR-FULL:v3p60/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r3.claim: Ibn Masud and other Companions report that Cain killed Abel with a rock while he slept, then learned burial by watching one raven bury another.
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن ابن مسعود وناس من الصحابة {فطوعت له نفسه قتل أخيه} ليقتله فراغ الغلام منه

DURR-FULL:v3p60/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Iblis taught Cain to kill by modeling the crushing of a bird’s head between stones.
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال: ابن آدم الذي قتل أخاه لم يدر كيف يقتله فتمثل له إبليس في صورة طير

DURR-FULL:v3p60/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r5.claim: Mujahid gives a similar report that Iblis taught the first murderer how to kill.
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r5.anchor: فعلمه القتل وأخرج عن مجاهد نحوه

DURR-FULL:v3p60/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r6.speaker: خيثمة
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r6.claim: Khaithama says the earth drank the victim’s blood and was cursed, so it never drank blood again.
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r6.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن خيثمة قال: لما قتل ابن آدم أخاه شفت الأرض دمه فلعنت فلم تشف الأرض دما بعد

DURR-FULL:v3p60/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r7.claim: Ali reports the Prophet locating the murder of Adam’s son on Mount Qasiyun in Damascus.
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r7.anchor: وأخرج ابن عساكر عن علي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال بدمشق جبل يقال له قاسيون فيه قتل ابن آدم أخاه

DURR-FULL:v3p60/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r8.speaker: كعب الأحبار
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r8.claim: Kaab, shown a flowing streak on Mount Dayr al-Murran by Amr ibn Khubayr, said this was the murder site and its blood, made by God as a sign to the worlds.
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r8.anchor: وأخرج ابن عساكر عن عمرو بن خبير الشعباني قال: كنت مع كعب الأحبار على جبل دير المران فرأى لجة سائلة في الجبل

DURR-FULL:v3p60/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r9.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r9.claim: In another report, Kaab identifies the blood on Mount Qasiyun as the blood of Adam’s son.
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r9.anchor: وأخرج ابن عساكر من وجه آخر عن كعب قال: إن الدم الذي على جبل قاسيون هو دم ابن آدم

DURR-FULL:v3p60/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r10.speaker: وهب
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r10.claim: Wahb says the earth absorbed Abel’s blood, so Cain cursed it; since Abel’s blood it has never absorbed blood, until the Resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r10.anchor: وأخرج ابن عساكر عن وهب قال: إن الأرض نشفت دم ابن آدم المقتول فلعن ابن آدم الأرض فمن أجل ذلك

DURR-FULL:v3p60/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r11.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن فضالة
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r11.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Fudala says God erased Cain’s reason and stripped his heart after the murder, leaving him wandering until death.
DURR-FULL:v3p60/r11.anchor: وأخرج نعيم بن حماد في الفتن عن عبد الرحمن بن فضالة قال: لما قتل قابيل هابيل مسح الله عقله وخلع فؤاده

DURR-FULL:v3p61/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p61/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p61/r1.claim: The Prophet says the first son of Adam to kill bears a share of every wrongful killing, since he established murder.
DURR-FULL:v3p61/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لاتقتل نفس ظلما

DURR-FULL:v3p61/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p61/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p61/r2.claim: The Prophet likewise says every wrongful killing leaves a share of its sin on the first murderer, who first instituted murder.
DURR-FULL:v3p61/r2.anchor: عن البراء بن عازب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ماقتلت نفس ظلما

DURR-FULL:v3p61/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p61/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
DURR-FULL:v3p61/r3.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr calls the first murderer the most wretched and says every bloodshed since his brother’s death adds something to his burden because he began the practice.
DURR-FULL:v3p61/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: إن أشقى الناس رجلا لابن آدم الذي قتل أخاه ما سفك دم في الأرض

DURR-FULL:v3p61/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p61/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p61/r4.claim: The Prophet names the she-camel killer of Thamud and Adam’s first murderous son among the three most wretched; every later bloodshed burdens the latter.
DURR-FULL:v3p61/r4.anchor: عن ابن عمرو قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أشقى الناس ثلاثة:

DURR-FULL:v3p61/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p61/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
DURR-FULL:v3p61/r5.claim: Ibn Amr reports that the first murderer receives half the punishment borne by the people of Hell.
DURR-FULL:v3p61/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير والبيهقي في شعب الإيمان عن ابن عمرو قال إنا لنجد ابن آدم القاتل يقاسم أهل النار قسمة صحيحة العذاب عليه شطر عذابهم

DURR-FULL:v3p61/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p61/r6.speaker: عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v3p61/r6.claim: A man named Abdullah recounts finding a dead town and a pool where Adam’s first bloodshed son hung upside down, unable to reach water; he identified himself when asked.
DURR-FULL:v3p61/r6.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي الدنيا كتاب من عاش بعد الموت من طريق عبد الله بن دينار عن أبي أيوب اليماني عن رجل من قومه يقال له عبد الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r6.claim: The فاء marks consequence and succession; طوعت portrays Cain's hesitation and inner struggle between envy and fear.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r6.anchor: على حدوث تردد في نفس قابيل ومغالبة بين دافع الحسد ودافع الخشية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r7.claim: An earlier event is elided, estimated as a long hesitation or waiting for an opportunity before his self made the murder seem easy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r7.anchor: أو فترصد فرصا فطوعت له نفسه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r8.claim: طوع means making something compliant; طاعة is the opposite of coercion, and تطويع is an effort to obtain compliance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r8.anchor: والطوع والطواعية : ضد الإكراه ، والتطويع : محاولة الطوع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r9.claim: The resistant murder is pictured as an intractable thing, while Cain's murderous impulse acts like an assistant that subdues it; this is a representational metaphor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r9.anchor: شبه قتل أخيه بشيء متعاص عن قابيل ولا يطيعه بسبب معارضة التعقل والخشية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r10.claim: The metaphor means that after resistance Cain's own self enticed him to kill his brother.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r10.anchor: فكان ( طوعت ) استعارة تمثيلية ، والمعنى الحاصل من هذا التمثيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r11.claim: The apparent repetition before فقتله is purposeful elaboration: it makes the killer's evil thoughts and hard heart vivid rather than merely saying he killed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r11.anchor: وكان مقتضى الإيجاز أن يحذف { فطوعت له نفسه قتل أخيه } ويقتصر على قوله { فقتله } لكن عدل عن ذلك لقصد تفظيع حالة القاتل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r12.claim: The elaboration stresses the cruelty of contemplating murder against someone he should have treated with mercy, so it is not pointless verbosity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p172/r12.anchor: بقتل من كان شأنه الرحمة به والرفق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p173/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p173/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p173/r1.claim: أصبح means صار, came to be.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p173/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p173/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p173/r2.claim: On one reading, Cain's loss is otherworldly: by killing his brother he became one who lost the afterlife.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p173/r2.anchor: أي صار بذلك القتل ممن خسر الآخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p173/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p173/r3.speaker: author
