IBNASHUR-FULL:v6p173/r3.claim: Alternatively, أصبح retains its literal morning sense: the murder happened in the morning, and worldly loss describes the killer's visible agitation, misery, and disappointed hope.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r1.speaker: جمهور القراء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r1.claim: The majority reading faṭawwaʿat portrays the rebellious, evil-commanding soul as making intrinsically difficult murder seem compliant and easy until Cain commits it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r1.anchor: قراءة الجمهور فطوعت والمعنى أن القتل في ذاته مستصعب عظيم على النفوس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r2.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن والجراح والحسن بن عمران وأبو واقد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r2.claim: These readers have faṭāwaʿat: Cain's hatred and envy made killing beckon while his soul resisted, until the soul yielded to the act.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بن أبي الحسن والجراح والحسن بن عمران وأبو واقد «فطاوعت» والمعنى كأن القتل يدعو إلى نفسه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r3.claim: One report says Cain waited for an opportunity, found Abel asleep among his sheep, and smashed his head with a stone.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r3.anchor: وروي أنه التمس الغرة في قتله حتى وجده نائما في غنمه فشدخ رأسه بحجر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r4.claim: Another report says Cain did not know how to kill until Iblis showed him by smashing a bird or other animal's head between two stones.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r4.anchor: وروي أنه جهل كيف يقتله فجاء إبليس بطائر أو حيوان غيره فجعل يشدخ رأسه بين حجرين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r5.claim: A report says Adam asked where Abel was; Cain denied knowing, and Adam cursed the ground for drinking Abel's blood, after which earth did not drink blood.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r5.anchor: والله إن دمه ليناديني من الأرض، اللهم العن أرضا شربت دم هابيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r6.claim: Another report says Adam did not smile for a hundred years until an angel greeted him and explained that bayyaka meant making him laugh.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r6.anchor: فقال آدم: ما بياك؟ قال أضحكك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r7.speaker: آدم عليه السلام
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r7.claim: A poem attributed to Adam laments that the land and its people changed, the earth became dusty and ugly, tastes and colors changed, and cheerful beautiful faces became scarce.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r7.anchor: تغيرت البلاد ومن عليها ... فوجه الأرض مغبر قبيح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r8.claim: Mujahid reports that the killer's leg was attached to his thigh until Judgment Day, his face turned toward the sun, with enclosures of fire and winter snow; the author says, if authentic, this is among his losses.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r8.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد أنه قال علقت إحدى رجلي القاتل بساقها إلى فخذها من يومئذ إلى يوم القيامة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r9.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr says the first killer shares the Hell-dwellers' punishment equally, bearing half their torment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r9.anchor: ومن خسرانه ما روي عن عبد الله بن عمرو أنه قال إنا لنجد ابن آدم القاتل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r10.claim: The author calls this authentic: every soul unjustly killed gives the first son of Adam a share of its guilt because he first instituted murder.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p179#2/r10.anchor: «ما قتلت نفس ظلما إلا كان على ابن آدم الأول كفل منها، وذلك أنه أول من سن القتل»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p180/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p180/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p180/r1.claim: Asbaha can describe all of someone's time, with part of a period standing for the whole; morning is singled out as the day's beginning and the start of activity and vigor.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p180/r1.anchor: فأصبح عبارة عن جميع أوقاته أقيم بعض الزمن مقام كله، وخص الصباح بذلك لأنه بدء النهار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p180/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p180/r2.speaker: الربيع بن ضبع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p180/r2.claim: The poet al-Rabi ibn Dab' illustrates this Arabic use of asbaha with a line beginning, “I have come to morning not bearing arms.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p180/r2.anchor: ومنه قول الربيع بن ضبع: أصبحت لا أحمل السلاح البيت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p180/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p180/r3.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p180/r3.claim: Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas likewise uses asbaha for a continuing state, saying that the sons of Asad then began to punish him for Islam.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p180/r3.anchor: ومنه قول سعد بن أبي وقاص، ثم أصبحت بنو أسد تعزرني على الإسلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p181/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p181/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p181/r9.claim: Scholars differ whether Cain was an unbeliever or a sinner; Ibn Atiyya says the apparent view is that he was a sinner.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p181/r9.anchor: واختلف العلماء في قابيل هل هو من الكفار أو من العصاة، والظاهر أنه من العصاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p181/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p181/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p181/r10.claim: A Prophetic report presents Adam's two sons as an example for the community: take the better one as a model and leave the worse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p181/r10.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال «إن الله ضرب لكم ابني آدم مثلا فخذوا من خيرهما ودعوا الشر»

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as Cain's soul following along with the killing of his brother.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r1.anchor: أحدها تابعته على قتل أخيه قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses the phrase as Cain's soul encouraging him to kill.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r3.claim: Qatada glosses the phrase as Cain's soul making the killing seem attractive.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r4.speaker: أبو الحسن الأخفش
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r4.claim: Abu al-Hasan al-Akhfash glosses the phrase as Cain's soul making the killing permissible to him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r4.anchor: والرابع رخصت له قاله أبو الحسن الأخفش

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r5.speaker: المبرد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r5.claim: The word is from ṭawʿ, willing compliance: Arabs say a thing came to someone willingly; al-Zajjaj transmits this from al-Mubarrad.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r5.anchor: أي أتاه طوعا حكاه الزجاج عن المبرد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r6.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r6.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses the verb as helping and yielding; the phrase my tongue does not yield means it does not comply.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة شايعته وانقادت له يقال لساني لا يطوع بكذا أي لا ينقاد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r7.claim: One report says Cain killed Abel by pelting him with stones; it comes through Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r7.anchor: أحدها أنه رماه بالحجارة حتى قتله رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r8.claim: Mujahid's report from Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi's from his elders say Cain struck Abel's head with a rock while he slept.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r8.anchor: والثاني ضرب رأسه بصخرة وهو نائم رواه مجاهد عن ابن عباس والسدي عن أشياخه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r9.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r9.claim: Ibn Jurayj says Satan demonstrated how to kill by crushing a bird's head between stones; Cain copied him, and Abel was twenty.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r9.anchor: قال ابن جريج لم يدر كيف يقتله فتمثل له إبليس وأخذ طائرا فوضع رأسه على حجر ثم شدخه بحجر آخر ففعل به هكذا وكان لهابيل يومئذ عشرون سنة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas places the killing on Mount Thawr.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r10.anchor: أحدها على جبل ثور قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r11.speaker: جعفر الصادق
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r11.claim: Ja'far al-Sadiq places the killing in Basra.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r12.speaker: ابن جرير الطبري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r12.claim: Ibn Jarir al-Tabari reports that the killing occurred near the pass of Hira.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r12.anchor: والثالث عند عقبة حراء حكاه ابن جرير الطبري

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas says Cain lost this world by angering his parents and becoming brotherless, and the next by angering God and going to Hell.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r13.anchor: أحدها من الخاسرين الدنيا والآخرة فخسرانه الدنيا أنه أسخط والديه وبقي بلا أخ

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r14.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r14.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Cain became one of those who lost their good deeds.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r14.anchor: والثاني أنه أصبح من الخاسرين الحسنات قال الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r15.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r15.claim: Qadi Abu Ya'la says Cain became one of those who lose themselves by destroying them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v2p337#2/r15.anchor: والثالث مني الخاسرين أنفسهم باهلاكهم إياها قاله القاضي أبو يعلى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r1.claim: His soul made the murder seem acceptable, suggested it to him, and emboldened him to kill after the admonition and warning.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r1.anchor: وسولت له نفسه، وشجعته على قتل أخيه فقتله، أي: بعد هذه الموعظة وهذا الزجر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر الباقر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r2.claim: Abu Jaʿfar al-Baqir, Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, reports that Cain killed Abel with an iron implement in his hand.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r2.anchor: وقد تقدم في الرواية عن أبي جعفر الباقر، وهو محمد بن علي بن الحسين: أنه قتله بحديدة في يده.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi, transmitting from Ibn Abbas, Abdullah, and a group of the Prophet’s Companions, says Cain pursued Abel into the mountains and smashed his sleeping head with a rock while Abel tended sheep, then left him exposed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r3.anchor: وقال السدي، عن أبي مالك وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r4.speaker: بعض أهل الكتاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r4.claim: Some People of the Book say Cain strangled and bit Abel as beasts of prey kill.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r4.anchor: وعن بعض أهل الكتاب: أنه قتله خنقا وعضا،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r5.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r5.claim: Ibn Jarir’s account says Cain did not know how to kill until Satan showed him by smashing an animal’s head between stones, after which Cain did the same to his brother.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن جرير (2) لما أراد أن يقتله جعل (3) يلوي عنقه، فأخذ إبليس دابة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r6.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r6.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam’s report says Satan showed Cain to crush Abel’s head with a rock; Satan then explained death to Hawwa, whose crying led Adam to decree wailing for her and her daughters and disavow it for himself and his sons.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p88#2/r6.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن وهب، عن عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم، عن أبيه قال: أخذ برأسه ليقتله،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r1.claim: Cain lost in both this world and the next; Ibn Kathir asks what loss could be greater.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r1.anchor: أي: في الدنيا والآخرة، وأي خسارة أعظم من هذه؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r2.claim: Ibn Masud reports the Prophet saying that every unjust killing gives the first son of Adam a share of its blood, since he was the first to institute murder; the report is transmitted by the hadith compilers except Abu Dawud.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "لا تقتل نفس ظلما، إلا كان على ابن آدم الأول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r3.claim: Mujahid says the killer’s leg was fastened to his other leg up to the thigh until Resurrection, with his face turned toward the sun and alternating enclosures of fire in summer and ice in winter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد: علقت إحدى رجلي القاتل بساقها إلى فخذها من يومئذ إلى يوم القيامة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r4.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr says the first killer shares the punishment of Hell’s inhabitants equally and bears half their torment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r4.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمرو: إنا لنجد ابن آدم القاتل يقاسم أهل النار قسمة صحيحة العذاب، عليه شطر عذابهم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r5.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr says the first killer is Hell’s most wretched person and receives a share of every unjust bloodshed from his brother’s murder onward because he first established killing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r5.anchor: عن حكيم بن حكيم، أنه حدث عن عبد الله بن عمرو أنه كان يقول:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r6.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r6.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi says every person murdered unjustly gives a share of the consequence to the first son of Adam and to Satan.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p89/r6.anchor: وقال إبراهيم النخعي: ما من مقتول يقتل ظلما، إلا كان على ابن آدم الأول والشيطان كفل منه.

JISHUMI:v3p1936/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r2.claim: طاع means to come willingly, انطاع to yield, and أطاع to carry out a command; طاوع means to agree with someone.
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r2.anchor: ويقال: طاع لفلان كذا: إذا أتاه طوعا، وانطاع: انقاد

JISHUMI:v3p1936/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r3.claim: In the phrase هو طوعة, cited in al-ʿAyn, the person follows or yields to another.
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r3.anchor: وفي العين: هو طوعة: إذا انقاد معه

JISHUMI:v3p1936/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r9.claim: The phrase means that his own soul helped him carry out the murder.
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r9.anchor: فطوعت له نفسه قتل أخيه قيل: ساعدته نفسه على قتل أخيه

JISHUMI:v3p1936/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r10.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r10.claim: Mujahid says his soul emboldened him to kill his brother.

JISHUMI:v3p1936/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r11.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r11.claim: Qatada says his soul made the murder seem attractive to him.
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r11.anchor: زينت له نفسه قتل أخيه، عن قتادة

JISHUMI:v3p1936/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r12.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود وأبو مالك
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r12.claim: They say Cain killed his brother while he slept by smashing his head with a rock.
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r12.anchor: قتل أخاه، وهو نائم، شدخ رأسه بصخرة، عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود وأبي مالك

JISHUMI:v3p1936/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r13.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r13.claim: Mujahid says Cain did not know how to kill; Satan demonstrated by smashing a bird's head, and Cain learned from him.
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r13.anchor: لم يدر كيف يقتله فظهر له إبليس وأخذ طيرا، وشدخ رأسه، فقتله، فتعلم منه، عن مجاهد

JISHUMI:v3p1936/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r14.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r14.claim: A view says this was the first killing among humanity.
JISHUMI:v3p1936/r14.anchor: وقيل: إنه أول قتيل في الناس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p659/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p659/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p659/r3.claim: His soul made the murder seem easy and wide open, from the idiom for pasture that has spread out.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p659/r3.anchor: فوسعته له ويسرته من طاع له المرتع اذا اتسع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p659/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p659/r4.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p659/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads fa-ṭāwaʿat; it may be a form-IV verb with the sense of faʿala, or mean that the murder called to Cain and his soul complied.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p659/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( فطاوعت ) وفيه وجهان ان يكون مما جاء من فاعل بمعنى فعل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p659/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p659/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p659/r5.claim: One account says Cain killed Abel at age twenty, either at ʿAqabat Ḥirāʾ or at Baṣra where the Great Mosque stands.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p659/r5.anchor: وقيل قتل وهو ابن عشرين سنة وكان قتله عند عقبة حراء وقيل بالبصرة في موضع المسجد الأعظم

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r7.claim: Ṭawwaʿat is explained as making an act seem easy: Mujahid says emboldened, Qatada says adorned, and another view says Cain's soul assisted him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r7.anchor: معنى طوعت أي فعلت من الطاعة , وفيه ثلاثة تأويلات : أحدها : يعني شجعت , وهو قول مجاهد . والثاني : يعني زينت , وهو قول قتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r8.claim: Abel was the first person killed on earth. Accounts say Cain did not know how to kill until Satan taught him, and that he murdered Abel by dropping a stone on his sleeping head.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r8.anchor: وكان هابيل أول من قتل في الأرض , وقيل إن قابيل لم يدر كيف يقتله حتى ظهر له إبليس فعلمه , وقيل إنه قتله غيلة

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r12.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r12.claim: A Prophetic report makes Adam's two sons a parable for this community: take the good of the better brother and leave the evil of the worse one.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r12.anchor: عن قتادة , عن الحسن , عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم , أنه قال : ( إن ابني آدم ضرب مثلا لهذه الأمة , فخذوا من خيرهما

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r13.claim: Exegetes disagree whether Cain was an unbeliever when he killed Abel or instead a wicked, sinful man.
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p29/r13.anchor: واختلف في قابيل هل كان عند قتل أخيه كافرا أو فاسقا ؟ فقال قوم كان كافرا , وقال آخرون بل كان رجل سوء فاسقا .

MUJAHID:v1p192/r3.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p192/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MUJAHID:v1p192/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas's report concludes that the farmer killed his brother and that all Adam's descendants came from that unbelieving son.
MUJAHID:v1p192/r3.anchor: فقتله صاحب الحرث فولد آدم كلهم من ولد ذلك الكافر

MUJAHID:v1p192/r7.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p192/r7.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p192/r7.claim: Mujahid says Cain's soul emboldened him to kill his brother.
MUJAHID:v1p192/r7.anchor: ﴿ فطوعت له نفسه ﴾ يقول شجعته نفسه على قتله

MUJAHID:v1p192/r9.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p192/r9.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p192/r9.claim: Mujahid links the killing to the likeness in 5:32 and to the warning in 4:93 about intentionally killing a believer.
MUJAHID:v1p192/r9.anchor: يقول الله عز وجل ﴿ من قتل نفسا بغير نفس أو فساد في الأرض فكأنما قتل الناس جميعا ﴾ قال هذا مثل قوله ﴿ ومن يقتل مؤمنا متعمدا فجزاؤه جهنم خالدا فيها ﴾

MUQATIL:5:28-31/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:5:28-31/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:5:28-31/r4.claim: His soul made the killing of his brother seem attractive to him; after the murder he became one of the losers.
MUQATIL:5:28-31/r4.anchor: { فطوعت له نفسه قتل أخيه } ، يقول: فزينت له نفسه قتل أخيه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p279#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279#3/r1.claim: His soul made the murder easy and acceptable; the phrase derives from a pasture being spacious for someone.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279#3/r1.anchor: فوسعته ويسرته من طاع له المرتع إذا اتسع

NASAFI-FULL:v1p279#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279#3/r2.claim: The murder took place either at ʿAqabat Ḥirāʾ or at Baṣra.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279#3/r2.anchor: فقتله ﴾ عند عقبة حراء أو بالبصرة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p279#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279#3/r3.claim: The murdered brother was twenty years old.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279#3/r3.anchor: البصرة والمقتول ابن عشرين سنة ﴿ فأصبح من الخاسرين

NASAFI-FULL:v1p279#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279#3/r4.claim: After the murder, Qābīl became one of the losers.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p279#3/r4.anchor: المقتول ابن عشرين سنة ﴿ فأصبح من الخاسرين

BURSEVI:v2p305/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p305/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p305/r2.claim: The verb comes from the expression for pasture becoming spacious: Cain's soul made killing his brother seem easy, open, and unconfined.
BURSEVI:v2p305/r2.anchor: {فطوعت له نفسه قتل أخيه} من طاع له المرتع إذا اتسع أي : وسعته وسهلته أي جعلته سهلا وهونته

BURSEVI:v2p305/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p305/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p305/r3.claim: Unlawful murder, especially of a brother, should appear wholly repugnant to reason and religious law; the commanding soul makes it easy by deploying its predatory, angry force.
BURSEVI:v2p305/r3.anchor: فإن قتل النفس بغير حق لا سيما قتل الأخ إذا تصوره الإنسان يجده شيئا عاصيا نافرا كل النفرة عن دائرة الشرع والعقل

BURSEVI:v2p305/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p305/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p305/r4.claim: The wording depicts the soul as making the act compliant to it, like a rebel made obedient; the added laam strengthens the connection though the sentence works without it.
BURSEVI:v2p305/r4.anchor: فكأن النفس صيرته كالمطيع لها بعد أن كان كالعاصي المتمرد عليها ويتم الكلام بدون اللام بأن يقال فطوعته نفسه قتل أخيه

BURSEVI:v2p305/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p305/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p305/r5.claim: The laam is an added connective; the clause is complete without it, just as one could say 'I preserved Zayd's property' without the laam construction.
BURSEVI:v2p305/r5.anchor: إلا أنه جيىء باللام لزيادة الربط كما في قولك حفظت لزيد ماله مع تمام الكلام بأن يقال حفظت مال زيد

BURSEVI:v2p305#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p305#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p305#2/r1.claim: One report says Cain did not know how to kill; the Devil demonstrated by smashing a bird or snake's head against a stone, and Cain copied him while Abel submitted. Another says Cain ambushed Abel in his sleep.
BURSEVI:v2p305#2/r1.anchor: قيل لم يدر قابيل كيف يقتل هابيل فتمثل إبليس وأخذ طائرا أو حية وضع رأسه على الحجر ثم شدخها بحجر آخر

BURSEVI:v2p305#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p305#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p305#2/r2.claim: The account places the killing near Mount Thawr, the pass of Hira, or Basra at the site of its great mosque, and says Abel was twenty years old.
BURSEVI:v2p305#2/r2.anchor: وهو مستسلم لا يستعصي عليه أو اغتاله وهو نائم وغنمه ترعى وذلك عند جبل ثور أو عقبة حراء أو بالبصرة في موضع المسجد الأعظم وكان لهابيل يوم قتله عشرون سنة

BURSEVI:v2p305#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p305#2/r3.speaker: بعض الكبار
BURSEVI:v2p305#2/r3.claim: A report from one of the great masters says Adam vomited what he had eaten on descending to earth; a poisonous tree grew from it, the snake ate the poison and became deadly, and Cain was conceived from what remained and became a murderer and corrupter.
BURSEVI:v2p305#2/r3.anchor: وعن بعض الكبار أن آدم لما هبط إلى الأرض تفكر فيما أكل فاستقاء فنبتت شجرة السم من قيئه فأكلت الحية ذلك السم

BURSEVI:v2p305#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p305#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p305#2/r4.claim: Cain lost both his religion and his worldly life.

BURSEVI:v2p305#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p305#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v2p305#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says Cain lost this world by angering his parents and remaining condemned until the Resurrection, and lost the next world through great punishment.
BURSEVI:v2p305#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : خسر دنياه وآخرته أما الدنيا فإنه أسخط لوالديه وبقي مذموما إلى يوم القيامة

BURSEVI:v2p308/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p308/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p308/r1.claim: In the inward reading, Cain's soul represents the lower self and his brother represents the heart; the self, the heart's greatest enemy, made killing it seem permissible.
BURSEVI:v2p308/r1.anchor: والإشارة في قوله : {فطوعت له نفسه} أي : نفس قابيل النفس طوعت له وجوزت {قتل أخيه} وهو القلب لأن النفس أعدى عدو القلب

BURSEVI:v2p308/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p308/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p308/r2.claim: Killing the heart makes the self lose in both worlds: here it forfeits spiritual arrivals, unveilings, unseen knowledge, witnessing, and intimacy, becoming ignorant and lost; the author links this to the short sura al-Asr.
BURSEVI:v2p308/r2.anchor: في قتل القلب خسارة النفس في الدنيا والآخرة أما في الدنيا فتحرم عن الواردات والكشوف والعلوم الغيبية

BURSEVI:v2p308/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p308/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p308/r3.claim: In the next world, killing the heart costs the self entry to the gardens, vision of the Generous Lord, and rescue from Hell and painful punishment.
BURSEVI:v2p308/r3.anchor: وأما في الآخرة فتخسر الدخول في جنات النعيم ولقاء الرب الكريم والنجاة من الجحيم والعذاب الأليم

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r1.claim: His soul enticed and emboldened him, making the killing seem easy and compliant.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r1.anchor: أي سولت وسهلت نفسه عليه الأمر وشجعته وصورت له أن قتل أخيه طوع سهل له

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r2.claim: طاع الشيء means it became easy and yielded; طوّعه له means someone made it easy for him.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r3.speaker: الهروي
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r3.claim: Al-Harawī treats طوّعت and أطاعت as equivalent; another parsing takes the phrase as طاوعته نفسه with the preposition omitted.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r3.anchor: قال الهروي: طوعت وأطاعت واحد يقال: طاع له كذا إذا أتاه طوعا.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r4.speaker: ابن جريج ومجاهد وغيرهما
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj, Mujāhid, and others report that Cain did not know how to kill; Satan demonstrated by smashing an animal’s head between stones, and Cain imitated him.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r4.anchor: وروي أنه جهل كيف يقتله فجاء إبليس بطائر أو حيوان غيره فجعل يشدخ رأسه بين حجرين

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r5.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd say Cain found Abel asleep and crushed his head with a stone; Ibn ʿAbbās locates it at a mountain bull in Mecca.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وابن مسعود: وجده نائما فشدخ رأسه بحجر وكان ذلك في ثور جبل بمكة

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r6.speaker: محمد بن جرير الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r6.claim: Muḥammad ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī reports another location: near the pass at Ḥirāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r6.anchor: وقيل: عند عقبة حراء حكاه محمد بن جرير الطبري.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r7.speaker: جعفر الصادق
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r7.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq places the killing in Basra at the site of the Great Mosque.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r7.anchor: وقال جعفر الصادق: بالبصرة في موضع المسجد الأعظم.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r8.claim: Abel was twenty years old when Cain killed him.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r8.anchor: وكان لهابيل يوم قتله قابيل عشرون سنة.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r9.claim: Another account says Cain instinctively knew how to kill because people understand that life ends and can be destroyed; he killed Abel with a stone in India.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r9.anchor: ويقال: إن قابيل كان يعرف القتل بطبعه لأن الإنسان وإن لم ير القتل فإنه يعلم بطبعه أن النفس فانية

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r10.claim: After killing Abel, Cain regretted it and wept; two crows fought, one killed the other, dug a grave, and buried it, which Cain copied.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r10.anchor: ولما قتله ندم فقعد يبكي عند رأسه إذ أقبل غرابان فاقتتلا فقتل أحدهما الآخر ثم حفر

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r11.claim: السوءة is explained either as the genitals or as the corpse of the murdered man.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r11.anchor: والسوءة يراد بها العورة، وقيل: يراد بها جيفة المقتول

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r12.claim: Cain fled to Aden in Yemen; Satan falsely said fire accepted Abel’s offering because Abel worshipped fire, and Cain built a fire-house, becoming the first fire-worshipper in one account.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r12.anchor: ثم إنه هرب إلى أرض عدن من اليمن، فأتاه إبليس وقال: إنما أكلت النار قربان أخيك

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that when Cain killed Abel while Adam was in Mecca, vegetation, food, fruit, water, and earth changed; Adam went to India and found Abel dead.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r13.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس، أنه لما قتله وآدم بمكة اشتاك الشجر، وتغيرت الأطعمة،

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r14.claim: An alternative account has Cain return to Adam, deny knowing Abel’s whereabouts, then hear Adam curse the land that drank Abel’s blood; it is said no land has drunk blood since.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r14.anchor: وقيل: إن قابيل هو الذي انصرف إلى آدم، فلما وصل إليه قال له: أين هابيل؟

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r15.speaker: مجاهد وسالم بن أبي الجعد
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r15.claim: Mujāhid and Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd report that Adam went a hundred years without laughing until an angel greeted him; “biyyāk” was explained as “make you laugh.”
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r15.anchor: ثم إن آدم بقي مائة سنة لم يضحك، حتى جاءه ملك فقال له: حياك الله يا آدم وبياك.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r16.claim: Seth, whose name means “gift of God,” was born when Adam was 130, five years after Abel’s death, as a successor in Abel’s place.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r16.anchor: ولما مضى من عمر آدم مائة وثلاثون سنة وذلك بعد قتل هابيل بخمس سنين ولدت له شيثا

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r17.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r17.claim: Muqātil says animals and birds had been tame around Adam, but after Abel’s murder they fled into the air, wilderness, and thickets.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30/r17.anchor: وقال مقاتل: كان قبل قتل قابيل هابيل السباع والطيور تستأنس بآدم

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r1.speaker: الثعلبي وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r1.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī and others transmit verses attributed to Adam mourning the changed land, dusty surface, altered tastes and colors, and diminished beauty.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r1.anchor: وروي أن آدم لما تغيرت الحال قال: تغيرت البلاد ومن عليها فوجه الأرض مغبر قبيح

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya notes that the transmitted poem has بشاشة in the accusative and suppresses tanwīn.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطية: هكذا هو الشعر بنصب «بشاشة» وكف التنوين.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r3.claim: Al-Qushayrī and others report Ibn ʿAbbās’s view that Adam did not compose poetry; his Syriac elegy for Abel passed to Seth and was later translated into Arabic verse by Yaʿrub ibn Qaḥṭān.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r3.anchor: قال القشيري وغيره قال ابن عباس: ما قال آدم الشعر، وإن محمدا والأنبياء كلهم في النهي عن الشعر سواء

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r4.speaker: أنس
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r4.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet said Tuesday was the day Eve menstruated and Adam’s son killed his brother.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r5.claim: A report in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim from ʿAbd Allāh says every unjust killing imposes blood-guilt on Adam’s first son because he initiated murder.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r5.anchor: وثبت في صحيح مسلم وغيره عن عبد الله قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r6.claim: By the same principle, Iblīs bears a share in sins involving prostration because he first disobeyed by it; religious innovators bear the burden of followers’ innovations.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r6.anchor: وبهذا الاعتبار يكون على إبليس كفل من معصية كل من عصى بالسجود لأنه أول من عصى به

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r7.claim: A Prophetic report says whoever initiates a good practice receives its reward and followers’ rewards, while whoever initiates an evil practice bears its sin and theirs.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r8.claim: The Prophet says the people he fears most for his community are its misleading leaders.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r9.claim: The first-offender principle applies only if the originator has not repented; Adam repented and was forgiven, so he bears no later sins for eating the forbidden thing.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r9.anchor: وهذا ما لم يتب الفاعل من تلك المعصية، لأن آدم عليه السلام كان أول من خالف في أكل ما نهي عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r10.claim: A further rationale is that Adam ate forgetfully, according to the soundest view; one who forgets is not sinful or accountable.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r10.anchor: ووجه آخر فإنه أكل ناسيا على الصحيح من الأقوال، كما بيناه في «البقرة» والناسي غير آثم

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r11.claim: The author refers to his earlier discussion in al-Baqara for the account of Adam’s forgetful eating.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r11.anchor: كما بيناه في «البقرة» والناسي غير آثم

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r12.claim: The episode shows envy can drive someone to destroy himself by killing his closest relative, the person most deserving of his care and protection.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r12.anchor: تضمنت هذه الآية البيان عن حال الحاسد، حتى أنه قد يحمله حسده على إهلاك نفسه

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r13.claim: The loser is one who has lost his good deeds.

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r14.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r14.claim: Mujāhid reports that Cain’s leg was fixed to his thigh until Resurrection, his face turned toward the sun, with a fire enclosure in summer and ice in winter.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r14.anchor: وقال مجاهد: علقت إحدى رجلي القاتل بساقها إلى فخذها من يومئذ إلى يوم القيامة

QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r15.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says if Mujāhid’s report is sound, it describes Cain’s worldly loss; otherwise the phrase encompasses loss in this world and the next.
QURTUBI-FULL:5:30#2/r15.anchor: قال ابن عطية: فإن صح هذا فهو من خسرانه الذي تضمنه قوله تعالى: { فأصبح من الخاسرين } وإلا فالخسران يعم خسران الدنيا والآخرة.

RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r1.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r1.claim: The commentators explain the phrase as meaning that Cain's soul made the murder easy for him; some instead say it emboldened him.
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون : سهلت له نفسه قتل أخيه

RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r2.claim: Razi explains that awareness of murder's enormity initially makes it seem resistant and impossible; the soul's whisperings make it easy, as though turning a rebellious act into an obedient one.
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r2.anchor: صار هذا الفعل سهلا عليه ، فكأن النفس جعلت بوساوسها العجيبة

RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r3.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r3.claim: The Mu'tazila object that if God creates everything, the beautifying and easing of the murder should be attributed to God, not to Cain's soul.
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r3.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : لو كان خالق الكل هو الله تعالى لكان ذلك التزيين

RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r4.claim: Razi replies that acts are attributed to their motives; since God creates those motives, He is the creator of all acts.
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r4.anchor: وجوابه : أنه لما أسندت الأفعال إلى الدواعي

RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r5.claim: A report says Cain did not know how to kill; Iblis demonstrated by striking a bird's head with a stone, and Cain later killed the sleeping Abel the same way.
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r5.anchor: قيل : لم يدر قابيل كيف يقتل هابيل ، فظهر له إبليس

RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r6.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r6.claim: The Prophet said that every unjust killing leaves a share of its bloodguilt on Adam's first son because he was the first to institute murder.
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r6.anchor: وعن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( لا تقتل نفس

RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says Cain lost both worlds: in this life he angered his parents and remained condemned until the Resurrection, and in the next he faces great punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس : خسر دنياه وآخرته ، أما الدنيا فهو أنه أسخط والديه

RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r8.claim: A report says Cain fled to Aden in Yemen; Iblis falsely told him fire had accepted Abel's offering because Abel worshiped it, so Cain built a fire temple and became the first fire-worshiper.
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r8.anchor: قيل : إن قابيل لما قتل أخاه هرب إلى عدن من أرض اليمن

RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r9.claim: Reports place Abel's killing when he was twenty, either at the Aqabat Hira or, according to another account, in Basra where the Great Mosque stands.
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r9.anchor: وروي أن هابيل قتل وهو ابن عشرين سنة

RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r10.claim: A report says Cain's formerly white body turned black; after he denied responsibility when Adam asked about Abel, Adam accused him, and Adam did not laugh for a hundred years afterward.
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r10.anchor: وروي أنه لما قتله اسود جسد وكان أبيض

RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r11.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r11.claim: Al-Kashshaf's author rejects the poem ascribed to Adam mourning Abel as a forged, faulty poem; Razi agrees, calling it too poor even for ignorant teachers and unworthy of Adam, whose knowledge God made a proof against the angels.
RAZI-FULL:v11p164/r11.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) يروى أنه رثاه بشعر
